<SUMMARY>The intelligence brief for June 26 - July 03, 2026, highlights significant developments in the semiconductor, AI, and critical minerals sectors, underpinned by escalating geopolitical tensions and trade dynamics. Global AI infrastructure expansion continues with new chip production and data center investments, while supply chain vulnerabilities remain a key concern, particularly regarding critical minerals and export controls. Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz persist, affecting energy markets, and discussions on fortifying supply chains are prominent across various regions. India and Japan are moving to fortify supply chains and investments are flowing into battery recycling and advanced technologies in India. West Asia is grappling with AI as a counterterrorism threat, and Iran's actions in the Strait of Hormuz are influencing global oil logistics.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>Iran has threatened a "forceful response" against ships not complying with its navigation terms for the Strait of Hormuz, escalating maritime security risks and impacting oil prices. Saudi Arabia warns that AI is becoming a counterterrorism threat, indicating an emerging security concern in the digital domain. Congo's order for cobalt miners to relinquish unused export quotas, coupled with fears of exporters losing quotas due to administrative glitches, signals potential instability in critical mineral supply chains. China's export controls and U.S. dependence are noted as contributing to a "gloomy future" for the EU semiconductor industry, underscoring significant geopolitical and economic risks.</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:**
Polibeli Group's shares rose over 12% as the company shifts focus to AI computing infrastructure in Southeast Asia. Chinese companies are prioritizing supply chain resilience, AI, and new markets for growth. The 4th China International Supply Chain Expo concluded in Beijing.

**Europe:**
Infineon opened the world's largest fab for power semiconductors and analog/mixed-signal technologies in Dresden, representing a 5 billion euro investment and creating 1,000 jobs. A British electronics retailer has warned of price increases due to a global memory chip shortage as AI data centers consume supply. The TRA has opened an anti-dumping investigation into imports of Linear Low-Density Polyethylene from the USA.

**Americas:**
The Nasdaq was up 26% in the first half of 2026, with AI stocks experiencing significant growth. Anthropic has redeployed its Claude Fable 5 AI model after U.S. export controls were lifted. Court documents revealed tensions between Anthropic and the Pentagon over Claude AI use. President Donald Trump highlighted Micron Technology Inc., which saw its stock rise after committing to donate $250 million. Nvidia is offering a new business model that involves taking a cut of AI cloud revenue on top of hardware sales, positioning itself as a financier for chip buyers. Cisco Systems is identified as an AI infrastructure play in the market. New York City and the eastern US are experiencing the hottest day of the year, straining electric grids. Binghamton University opened a state-of-the-art cleanroom to support advanced research and workforce training.</EXEC>
<LITHO>

**Asia:**
A "Diplomat – Asia-Pacific" report discussed parsing signal from noise regarding China’s EUV Lithography Progress.

**Europe:**
A "Diplomat – Asia-Pacific" report discussed parsing signal from noise regarding China’s EUV Lithography Progress, reflecting global interest in advanced lithography capabilities.</LITHO>
<REE>

**Asia:**
China is investing $210 million to build a diamond semiconductor supply chain. The EU and Beijing have agreed to monitor trade flows and improve access to rare earth materials.

**Africa:**
Africa holds a quarter of the world's critical minerals powering AI and clean energy, but less than 10% of mining projects are moving ahead. Congo has ordered cobalt miners to give up unused export quotas, a move also reported as a seizure of quotas for the national reserve. Nigeria is focusing on its battery supply chain with the largest lithium processing plant in West Africa. DR Congo, South Africa, Morocco, and Guinea are noted for having significant mineral reserves. Congo cobalt exporters fear losing quotas due to administrative glitches.

**Americas:**
IperionX completed the strategic Camden Acquisition, unlocking ultra-high-grade critical minerals to accelerate the U.S. supply chain, with Camden surface stockpiles showing grades up to 23% THM for titanium, zircon, and heavy rare earth feedstocks. Consolidated Lithium Metals announced results for the Updated Preliminary Economic Assessment for the Kwyjibo Underground Mining Project, focusing on rare earth elements.

**Europe:**
The Greek Minister of Energy stated that the first exploratory well for hydrocarbon exploration is expected in mid-February 2027 at the Asopos site. The EU and Beijing have agreed to monitor trade flows and improve access to rare earth materials.</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:**
The EU ended a customs exemption for low-value imports from China, which previously accounted for 91% of approximately 16 million daily packages arriving in the EU. Moolenaar’s bipartisan bill aims to protect U.S. export controls for AI chips. China's export controls and U.S. dependence are reported to cause a "gloomy future" for the EU semiconductor industry. Taiwan raided Supermicro and two supply-chain partners in a widening Nvidia smuggling probe, with nine sites hit and six people summoned for questioning.

**Europe:**
Brussels ended a customs exemption for low-value imports from China while agreeing with Beijing to monitor trade flows and improve access to rare earth materials. The EU semiconductor sector is vulnerable to China's export controls.

**Americas:**
Anthropic's advanced Claude Fable 5 AI model was redeployed after U.S. export controls were lifted. Court documents revealed tensions between Anthropic and the Pentagon over Claude AI use.</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Asia:**
Space Data Centers are being explored as a solution for AI's energy problems, with orbiting servers potentially powering future AI infrastructure.</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>

**Asia:**
Innoscience secured the removal of court-enjoined Infineon GaN products from display at electronica China 2026. D-Matrix announced its Corsair AI inference accelerator is in full production and will begin shipping this month. Polibeli Group is shifting to AI computing infrastructure in Southeast Asia, with shares rising 13%. Anthropic is in talks with Samsung Electronics to build custom AI chips, a partnership also discussed in U.S. media. China is making a $210 million investment to build a diamond semiconductor supply chain. Beyond GPUs, AI-driven shortages are impacting chip materials and components.

**Africa:**
The South Korean AI Rout contributed to dragging emerging stocks to a three-week low.

**Europe:**
Pilot Photonics was awarded €10.4 million from the European Innovation Council for integrated photonics. Infineon opened the world's largest fab for power semiconductors and analog/mixed-signal technologies in Dresden, with a 5 billion euro investment. Anthropic is in talks with Samsung Electronics to build custom AI chips. SK Hynix plans to spend $64 billion on memory chip plants as part of a broader AI investment.

**Americas:**
Anthropic integrated Claude AI agents into Microsoft Teams and Azure Foundry. Trump highlighted Micron Technology Inc., which committed to donating $250 million. Intel Foundry broke ground on a Santa Clara facility. Air Liquide is operating two gas production units for SK hynix chips. Anthropic is weighing a Samsung partnership for custom AI chips, eyeing Samsung Foundry. Mexico's semiconductor adhesive paste and film market is under analysis.

**Oceania:**
Pact Group supports mandatory packaging rules in Australia, making producers responsible for disposal and recovery of materials.</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>
BatX Energies secured ₹105 crore in Series A funding, which will be used to expand battery recycling capacity and develop a domestic critical minerals supply chain. India and Japan are moving to fortify supply chains and enhance collaboration on robust supply chains in the Indo-Pacific, acknowledging New Delhi's economic influence in addressing the "weaponisation of economies." A significant leak of Apple’s confidential iPhone 18 Pro schematics occurred due to a cyberattack on Tarta Electronics, a key manufacturing partner in India. Functional & Innovative Foods filed its DRHP with Sebi for an IPO to fund capacity expansion, debt repayment, subsidiary investment, and working capital needs. NITI Aayog is prioritizing recycling as India’s fastest route to critical minerals security, as discussed at the ICC’s 15th Minerals & Metals Forum. Japan announced 129 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with India at the Japan-India Joint Economic Forum, highlighting growing investments in advanced technologies, clean energy, and semiconductors.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
Indirect talks between Iran and the U.S. concluded in Doha without a resolution, with Iran threatening a "forceful response" against ships that do not comply with its terms for navigating the Strait of Hormuz. Crude oil prices are crashing on reports of Strait of Hormuz flows recovering, despite Iran's refusal to negotiate peace with U.S. envoys. The U.S. and Oman are seeking alternatives to Iran’s tolls on the Strait of Hormuz. Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shaibani visited Lebanon for meetings, rejecting a military role but open to talks with Hezbollah in Lebanon. Edge226 acquired AnyClip Ltd. to enhance AI-powered cross-channel performance marketing. Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) has asked asset management funds to form consortiums for bids on a planned $7 billion oil pipeline deal. Saudi Arabia warns that AI is becoming a counterterrorism threat. Israel is extending aid without borders through an AI humanitarian push. Turkey and Israel are considering trading energy. Saudi Arabia requires an overland route to global energy markets. The DCIIS UAE 2026 concluded in Dubai, focusing on resilient, sustainable, and AI-ready data center infrastructure. The UAE and US are deepening AI partnership under the Pax Silica framework. Middle East airports are expanding AI and biometric technology. XRG is increasing its Rio Grande LNG stake, strengthening US-UAE energy ties.
</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming period will likely see continued intense competition in the semiconductor and AI sectors, marked by strategic partnerships, such as Anthropic's discussions with Samsung, and significant investments in manufacturing capacity by entities like Infineon and SK Hynix. The emphasis on supply chain resilience, particularly for critical minerals and AI chips, will drive further state actions and private sector adjustments. Geopolitical tensions, exemplified by Iran's stance on the Strait of Hormuz and China's export controls, will remain a key factor influencing global trade and energy security. The dual nature of AI, driving both economic growth and new security challenges such as counterterrorism threats, necessitates ongoing vigilance and strategic development.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
